cold_open.hook: Amazon just jumped 13.7% while Apple cratered 9.2%—the market is literally choosing winners and losers in real time.

markets.macro_note: Broad market flat but bifurcated: mega-cap earnings winners surge, losers crater; volatility ticking up on geopolitical premium.

big_story.story_title: Apple heads for $460 billion wipeout with its stock seeing worst post-earnings drop in 13 years
big_story.angle: Apple's worst post-earnings drop in 13 years isn't just a stock move—it's a referendum on whether the iPhone is still a growth engine or a cash cow that's run out of runway, and what that means for the entire premium consumer tech narrative.

quick_hits.angle: Amazon's 13.7% pop on earnings isn't just a beat—it's validation that AWS + advertising + logistics moat is now genuinely unchallenged; the stock is pricing in a decade of margin expansion.
Tesla selling China operations ahead of a SpaceX merger is the kind of financial engineering that only works if you're Elon and the market is willing to suspend disbelief for another quarter.
Exxon and Chevron profits surge on Iran war oil spike—the geopolitical risk premium is real money, and it's flowing to the one sector everyone said was dying.
Sony ditching discs despite backlash is a bet that streaming + digital ownership is now inevitable; the last physical media holdouts are finally folding.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Consumer companies staying private longer to avoid the IPO road—turns out going public is now the financial equivalent of a bad Yelp review that never goes away.
